caption: The drawing consists of a detailed technical illustration of a tall, narrow banjo clock, rendered in black ink or pencil on a beige background. The clock features a round face with Roman numerals marking the hours, and “E. GRAHAM” inscribed at the center. The clock face is topped with a spindle and finial ornament. Below the face, the clock body tapers inward and then flares outward toward the rectangular base. Measurements and dimensions are indicated with arrows and annotations; the overall length is given as 28-3/4 inches and the width as 10 inches. Additional labeled elements include a carved and gilded spindle, floral and scrollwork motifs, an ornamental support, and a panel design shown on the right side, as well as a detailed border design on the left. A small circular inset displays a landscape scene with trees, a river, a sailboat, and hills, noted as a “landscape on face.” The rectangular base includes a bordered panel marked for a 5” x 7” area. The upper right corner bears the label “BANJO CLOCK - 1796 ONEIDA HISTORICAL SOCIETY UTICA, N.Y.” Handwritten notations and signatures appear in blue at the lower left corner.
title: Banjo Clock
